lesson_title: Silver Fur, Pickpockets and Six Electron Coins: Redox
hook_text: Dip copper wire in a clear solution and it grows silver fur while the liquid turns blue. That's a robbery in progress.
clip_script: Stand a coil of copper wire in a colourless silver nitrate solution. Glittering silver crystals fur the wire, and the solution slowly turns blue. What you are watching is coins changing pockets. Every atom keeps an electron account, and the audit says: copper went from zero to plus two — it PAID two electron coins, and the blue colour is the copper ion announcing itself. Each silver ion went from plus one to zero — it COLLECTED a coin, and the crystals are the receipts. Paying is oxidation, collecting is reduction. OIL RIG. Now the naming twist that catches everyone: the silver ion — the taker — is called the OXIDISING agent, and it ends up reduced. Not backwards. Agents are named for what they do to the OTHER species. The pickpocket is named by the victim's loss. Silver caused copper's oxidation, so silver is the oxidising agent — and taking electrons means being reduced yourself. Say it until it is boring: oxidising agent gets reduced, reducing agent gets oxidised. And next year, this exact trade runs through a wire — and the passing coins become the current out of a battery.
visual_style: Macro shot of copper wire furring over with silver crystals as blue creeps into the liquid; electron coins hopping from copper's open ledger to silver's; a pickpocket silhouette for the naming beat; the beaker morphing into a battery at the close.
mood: True-crime playful — a chemical robbery narrated like a heist.
pacing: Slow visual open on the crystals and colour, quick ledger beats, the naming twist, battery punchline.
